events.title: Athens destroyed
events.text: The Athenian expedition is annihilated at the Assinarus river; the survivors die in Syracuse's quarries.

events.title: Hired too late
events.text: Eight hundred Campanian horsemen hired by Sicily's Chalcidian cities for Athens arrive to find the war lost.

events.title: Carthage hires them
events.text: Carthage buys the Campanians horses, pays them well and sends them to defend its ally Segesta.

events.title: Selinus falls
events.text: Hannibal Mago's army storms Selinus in nine days and kills or enslaves its people.

events.title: Himera destroyed
events.text: Hannibal razes Himera and kills three thousand prisoners where his grandfather fell in 480 BC.

events.title: Acragas falls
events.text: Campanians fight for Acragas until bought off for fifteen talents; the starving city is abandoned to Carthage.

events.title: Gela abandoned
events.text: Dionysius fails to relieve Gela and evacuates Gela and Camarina before Himilco's army.

events.title: Peace with Carthage
events.text: A treaty leaves Carthage master of western and southern Sicily and Dionysius tyrant of Syracuse.

events.title: Rescue of a tyrant
events.text: Besieged by rebels, Dionysius calls in twelve hundred Campanian cavalry who cut their way to him.

events.title: Entella seized
events.text: Received as fellow citizens, the Campanians kill Entella's men by night and marry their wives.

events.title: Catana handed over
events.text: Dionysius sells the people of Catana into slavery and gives their city to his Campanians.

events.title: Motya sacked
events.text: Dionysius' siege engines and catapults take Carthage's island city of Motya.

events.title: Messana razed
events.text: Himilco's army takes Messana and levels it on the way to Syracuse.

events.title: Plague at Syracuse
events.text: Plague ravages Himilco's besieging army; he buys his own escape and abandons his mercenaries.

events.title: Campanians to Aetna
events.text: Dionysius moves his Campanians from Catana to Aetna, on the volcano's slopes.

events.title: Rhegium starved
events.text: After an eleven-month siege Dionysius takes Rhegium and sells its people into slavery.

events.title: Dionysius dies
events.text: The tyrant who ruled Syracuse for thirty-eight years dies; his son inherits a fragile empire.

events.title: Bruttian league
events.text: The Bruttians, said by Diodorus to be mostly runaway slaves, rise and make Consentia their capital.

events.title: Capua turns to Rome
events.text: Threatened by the Samnites, Capua surrenders itself to Rome, drawing Rome into Campania.

events.title: The Crimisus
events.text: Timoleon routs a Carthaginian army in a thunderstorm on the Crimisus river.

events.title: Aetna's end
events.text: Timoleon storms Aetna and puts its Campanian settlers to death.

events.title: Caudine Forks
events.text: The Samnites trap a Roman army in a mountain pass and send it under the yoke.

events.title: Agathocles
events.text: A potter's son turned general seizes Syracuse with his mercenaries and kills thousands of opponents.

events.title: War in Africa
events.text: Blockaded in Syracuse, Agathocles lands an army near Carthage and burns his own ships.

events.title: Venusia
events.text: Rome founds a Latin colony of thousands of settlers at Venusia, between Samnium and Apulia.

events.title: Agathocles dies
events.text: The king of Syracuse dies; his Campanian mercenaries are told to leave the city.

events.title: Messana stolen
events.text: Admitted as guests, Agathocles' Campanians kill or expel Messana's men and take their wives and homes.

events.title: Gela destroyed
events.text: Phintias, tyrant of Acragas, razes Gela and moves its people to his new city on the coast.

events.title: Heraclea
events.text: Pyrrhus of Epirus, called in by Taras, defeats a Roman army with his phalanx and elephants.

events.title: Rhegium seized
events.text: Four thousand Campanians sent by Rome to guard Rhegium kill or drive out its citizens.

events.title: Asculum
events.text: Pyrrhus wins a second costly victory over Rome in Apulia.

events.title: Pyrrhus at Eryx
events.text: Crossing to Sicily, Pyrrhus storms the mountain fortress of Eryx; only Lilybaeum resists him.

events.title: Maleventum
events.text: Rome checks Pyrrhus at Maleventum; he sails home to Greece.

events.title: Hiero elected
events.text: The Syracusan army chooses the officer Hiero as its general.

events.title: Taras surrenders
events.text: Taras hands itself over to Rome; Rome now commands Italy's south.

events.title: Rhegium retaken
events.text: Rome besieges and storms Rhegium and returns it to its surviving citizens.

events.title: Executions in the Forum
events.text: About three hundred captured mutineers are flogged and beheaded in the Roman Forum.

events.title: Beneventum
events.text: Rome plants a Latin colony at Maleventum and renames it Beneventum.

events.title: Longanus river
events.text: Hiero crushes the Mamertine army near Mylae and is hailed as king.

events.title: A Punic garrison
events.text: The Mamertines let a Carthaginian garrison into Messana's citadel, then turn to Rome.

events.title: Rome votes for war
events.text: The assembly votes to help the Mamertines; consul Appius Claudius crosses the strait.

events.title: Volsinii destroyed
events.text: Rome destroys Etruscan Volsinii and moves its people to a new site.

eras: Rhegium, Hiero and the Road to War
chartNote: Share of the area of today's provinces of southern Italy, Sicily and Sardinia, by the power that dominated each province's main city or people. Regions are today's boundaries; ancient cities and spheres of influence had none, and alliances shifted every few years, so the map is a simplification. Entella, held by Campanians from 404 BC, lay inside Carthage's zone and is shown as part of it.
